To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the behavior of the proton structure function at very high- energies is given by a universal function of the scaling variable x and that the proton radius is given by the square root of the inverse of the structure function at x= 1.
at very high energy the behavior of cross-sections is dominated by the behavior of the scattering amplitudes in the forward direction.
(1) the behavior of the cross section at high energies depends on the behavior of the amplitude at high energies and (2) the amplitude in the forward direction is approximately independent of energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the behavior of cross sections at very high energies.
the study of the properties of hadrons, the building blocks of matter, in the framework of the Standard Model and its possible extensions.
the study of the strong interactions at the highest energies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at high-energies, the cross-sections of the second order are of the order of the square of the logarithm of energy, which is a very small quantity.
the cross section for the scattering of a proton with a photon is approximately energy independent at very high energies.
the cross section of a process is the square of a quantity that is called the amplitude.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the high-energy behavior of the forward amplitude is determined by the high-energy behavior (in the limit of the energy tending to infinity) of the elastic amplitude at zero angle.
the cross-sections of hadrons are not energy independent at high energies, but rather they grow with the energy.
the cross section of a proton-proton scattering is the sum of the elastic and inelastic cross sections.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cross-sections of processes that have a large number of final particles are not suppressed by the phase-space factor as much as one would naively expect.

, at very high energies, the cross-sections of all processes involving hadrons are of the dimension of inverse of mass, and are approximately energy independent, and are approximately the same for all processes.
the cross-section of the proton in the forward direction is not energy independent at high energies, but grows with energy as the fourth power of the center-of-mass energy.
